item.title: On the Hodge conjecture for hyper-K\"ahler varieties of generalized Kummer type of dimension divisible by four
item.description: arXiv:2610.31740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Hodge conjecture for all hyper-K\"ahler varieties of generalized Kummer type of dimension $2n$ with $n+1$ a prime number, and all powers of these varieties. For any variety $X$ of generalized Kummer type of dimension divisible by 4, we show that the Lefschetz standard conjecture for $X$ implies the Hodge conjecture for $X$ and all its powers.
item.dc:creator: Salvatore Floccari, Lie Fu

item.title: Chern-Schwartz-MacPherson classes of symmetric powers and applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.31826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Chern-Schwartz-MacPherson class $c_{SM}(X)$ is defined in the Chow group $A_*(X)$ of a scheme $X$, and generalizes $c(T_X)\cap [X]$ if $X$ is smooth. In this paper we independently compute $c_{SM}(S^nX)\in A_*(S^nX)$ modulo $n!$ torsion; we use this result to compute the pushforward to $S^nX$ of $c_{SM}(Quot^n_X(E))$ (and in particular $c_{SM}(Hilb^n X)$) when $X$ is smooth and $E$ is a vector bundle on $X$. Finally, when $X$ is smooth and complete of dimension $3$ we propose a refined version of the the MNOP conjecture that computes the image of the pushforward of $[Hilb^n X]^{vir}$ to $A_0(S^nX)$ and prove it modulo $n!$ torsion when $X$ is Calabi-Yau.
item.dc:creator: Barbara Fantechi, Lothar Goettsche

item.title: Comparison of Logarithmic Hochschild Homologies
item.description: arXiv:2610.31879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a comparison morphism $\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Rog}}\to\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Ols}}$ between Rognes' logarithmic Hochschild homology and Olsson's logarithmic Hochschild homology which generalizes the comparison between Gabber's log cotangent complex $\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{Gab}}$ and Olsson's log cotangent complex $\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{Ols}}.$ In particular, Olsson's comparison is recovered as the first associated graded piece of our comparison morphism $\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Rog}}\to\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Ols}}.$ In the development of this comparison, we also prove a descent result for the cotangent complex generalizing a result of Bhatt, and construct a notion of HKR completed Hochschild homology for a general morphism of derived stacks which is functorial in the morphism and generalizes existing constructions of Hochschild homology when the base is affine.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Stahl

item.title: Kashiwara's Lemma for Potent D-modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.32003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On stacks there is a richer version of $\mathcal{D}$-modules---called $\textit{potent }\mathcal{D}\textit{-modules}$---which decompletes at equivariant parameters, in the same sense that genuine equivariant $K$-theory decompletes equivariant cohomology. In this paper, we prove a ``genuine'' version of Kashiwara's lemma for $\mathcal{D}$-modules. Namely, we show that for a broad class of geometric stacks $X$, if $Z \subset X$ is a closed substack, the category $\mathcal{D}^{\mathrm{pot}}(Z)$ of potent $\mathcal{D}$-modules on $Z$ is equivalent under pushforward to the category $\mathcal{D}^{\mathrm{pot}} _Z(X)$ of potent $\mathcal{D}$-modules on $X$ with support contained in $Z$.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Erlikhman, Kendric Schefers

item.title: Tropical cohomology for band schemes over the tropical hyperfield
item.description: arXiv:2610.32016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define tropical band varieties as $\mathbf{T}$-reductions of separated finitely presented $\mathbf{T}$-band schemes. We construct a faithful functor from the category of tropical band varieties to the category of extended polyhedral spaces in the sense of Gross--Shokrieh. As a byproduct, we show that tropical cohomology can be defined functorially on tropical band varieties.
item.dc:creator: Seungkyu Lee

item.title: On polarizations of affine Calabi--Yau varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.32036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(X, \Omega)$ be an affine Calabi--Yau variety, by which we mean a klt affine variety $X$ with a non-vanishing algebraic volume form $\Omega$. In connection with complete Calabi--Yau metrics of Euclidean volume growth on $(X, \Omega)$, we study algebraic aspects of polarizations of $X$ given by a negative valuation. We show that such a valuation is finitely generated with a klt degeneration if and only if $X$ admits a dlt log Fano type compactification, generalizing a compactification considered by Tian--Yau. We further give a valuative criterion detecting K-semistability of the degeneration by a negative valuation.
item.dc:creator: Yueqiao Wu

item.title: Power Sum Varieties over Finite Fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.32056v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a family of affine algebraic varieties over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ defined by systems of power sum polynomials. Our main goal is to investigate their geometric and arithmetic properties, with particular emphasis on the structure and dimension of their singular loci. Using tools from the theory of symmetric polynomials and generalized Vandermonde determinants, we establish explicit conditions under which these varieties are complete intersections and prove that, in a broad range of parameters, their singular loci have codimension at least two. As a consequence, we derive normality and irreducibility results for both the affine varieties and their projective closures. Building on this geometric analysis, we obtain estimates for the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points and deduce effective existence results for solutions of systems of symmetric power sum equations over finite fields. Finally, we apply these results to the study of Waring's problem and to the analysis of the cost of computing a $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational point of such systems.
item.dc:creator: Nardo Gim\'enez, Juan Francisco Gottig, Miguel Palacios, Mariana P\'erez, Melina Privitelli

item.title: Motivic local density of isolated singularities of algebraic varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.32416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The goal of this paper is to compute the motivic local density of an isolated singularity of an algebraic variety, in order to explain its link with algebraic multiplicity. We compute the density as the residue in 1 of a Zeta function associated to normalized local volumes and we use a resolution of the singularity to get the formula.
item.dc:creator: Sidonie Ratajczak

item.title: Reflection groups on smooth projective threefolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.32450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $Y$ be a smooth projective threefold with $H^2(Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)=0$ and unobstructed deformations. We define reflection groups $W_Y^{sm}$ and $W_Y^{big}$ canonically associated to $Y$, acting on the nef, resp. movable cone of a very general deformation of $Y$. If $-K_Y$ is nef, we show that $\mathrm{Nef}(Y)\cap\mathrm{Big}(Y)$ (resp. $\overline{\mathrm{Mov}}(Y)\cap\mathrm{Big}(Y)$) is a fundamental domain for the action of the corresponding group on the big part of the generic cone. This generalizes work of Wilson and Lutz on Calabi--Yau threefolds. The group $W_Y^{big}$ recovers and gives a deformation-theoretic explanation for the Weyl group action on divisor classes of point blowups of $\mathbb P^3$ studied by Dolgachev--Ortland and Mukai.
item.dc:creator: Wendelin Lutz

item.title: Jacobian layers and higher Milnor sequences: rigidity, stabilization, and log-concavity
item.description: arXiv:2610.32523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f$ be an isolated hypersurface singularity and let $J(f)$ be its Jacobian ideal. We study the higher Milnor numbers $\mu_k(f)=\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal O_n/\mathfrak m^kJ(f).$ Our main result concerns an ordinary semi-homogeneous singularity $f=f_r+f_{r+1}+\cdots$, where the projective hypersurface defined by $f_r$ is smooth. We prove that $\mu_k(f)=\mu_k(f_r) \qquad\text{for every }k\geq0.$ This gives the equal-weight case of a conjecture of Shi, Yau, and Zuo. The main algebraic input is the common-order case of the Valabrega--Valla criterion. From it, we obtain the graded Jacobian module and the exact intersection formula. As a consequence, we obtain a closed formula for $\mu_k$ and determine the sharp stabilization index of $\mathfrak m^kJ(f)$. We also determine the optimal uniform range in which the Tjurina formula holds for all ordinary semi-homogeneous germs with fixed $n$ and $r$. We next consider the log-concavity property. For ordinary semi-homogeneous singularities, the higher Milnor sequence has an initial log-convex part and a log-concave tail. For an arbitrary isolated hypersurface singularity in $n\geq2$ variables, both the higher Milnor and higher Tjurina sequences are eventually strictly log-concave. In the plane curve case, we prove that the log-concavity defects change sign at most once, and we characterize the sequences which are log-concave at every positive index. Finally, we give examples showing that the higher Milnor sequence does not determine the contact-equivalence class.
item.dc:creator: Zhiwen Liu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Mingyi Zhang

item.title: Deformations of cohomology classes and spectral sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.32593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study spectral sequences as an obstruction theory to deforming cohomology classes via the Rees construction. A filtered complex is interpreted as an equivariant family over the affine line, in which higher spectral sequence differentials arise as obstructions to lifting cohomology classes through infinitesimal neighborhoods of the special fibre. This leads to various geometric and module-theoretic degeneration criteria. We give various applications to $\mathrm{Ext}$ spectral sequences for complex Lagrangians and the formality results of Melani-Rubi\'o amongst others. For double complexes, we revisit the Khovanov-Qi decomposition on the Rees side and introduce a two-parameter Rees construction over the affine plane. The higher differentials of the two associated spectral sequences correspond to torsion modules supported on the thickened coordinate axes. We obtain degeneration criteria in terms of these modules and an intrinsic characterisation of the $\partial\bar\partial$-lemma.
item.dc:creator: Borislav Mladenov

item.title: On quasi-Albanese morphisms for log canonical Calabi-Yau pairs II
item.description: arXiv:2610.32782v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Centering on quasi-Albanese morphisms, we prove several structural theorems for Calabi-Yau pairs.
item.dc:creator: Yiming Zhu

item.title: $G_0$ of complete split toric varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.32831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves for complete split toric surfaces having a smooth 2-dimensional cone in its fan. We show that it is free abelian, of rank equal to the number of rays in the fan. We give a partial generalization of this to all complete split toric varieties.
item.dc:creator: Zeyu Shen

item.title: Kazhdan--Lusztig Polynomials for permutations with $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=3$ and Irreducible Singular Locus
item.description: arXiv:2610.32832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)$ for permutations $w$ such that $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=3$ and the Schubert variety $X_w$ has irreducible singular locus. Let $h=h(w)$ be the minimum height $w(a)-w(d)$ of a $3412$-occurrence in $w$ at positions $a<b<c<d$, with $h=1$ when no such occurrence exists. We show that $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)=1+q^h+q^{h+1}$ if exactly one of the patterns $3412$ and $4231$ occurs, and $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)=1+q+q^h$ if both patterns occur. In the latter case, $h>1$. This proves the irreducible singular locus case of a 2009 conjecture of Billey and Weed.
item.dc:creator: Gaston Burrull, Zhitong Alex Li, Shixuan Zeng

item.title: Rank 3 curve semistable Higgs bundles: the nilpotent case
item.description: arXiv:2610.32900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Higgs bundle on a smooth complex projective variety is curve semistable if its pullback to every smooth projective curve is semistable. A 2008 conjecture asserts that this is equivalent to slope semistability for some polarization plus vanishing discriminant. One direction is known, the converse holds in rank two, and Huang recently gave a rank-four counterexample. We prove the conjecture for rank three nilpotent Higgs bundles in any dimension. We treat separately the two possible cases: if the Higgs field $\phi$ is nilpotent of order two, there is a divisorial component of a Higgs Grassmannian where nefness of the normalized tautological class forces the discriminant to vanish; otherwise, $\phi$ is regular nilpotent, and then the canonical kernel flag, commutativity and Bogomolov's lemma on line subbundles of the cotangent bundle complete the proof.
item.dc:creator: Ugo Bruzzo, Beatriz Gra\~na Otero

item.title: The Verra involution on special cubic fourfolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.32952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a detailed study of the Hodge theory, geometry and derived categories of Verra fourfolds, and their relationship with twisted K3 surfaces and cubic fourfolds. We classify Brauer classes of Verra type on K3 surfaces of degree 2, and use this to derive an explicit counting formula for Fourier--Mukai partners of a large class of Verra fourfolds. We develop the basic theory of cohomology of Verra fourfolds and apply it to prove a derived Torelli theorem for a large class of Verra fourfolds. As an application, we prove that L-equivalent Verra fourfolds in this class are Fourier--Mukai partners, and conjecture that this implication holds for all Verra fourfolds. We then give a construction of cubic fourfolds birational to Verra fourfolds. The construction yields examples of cubic and Verra fourfolds whose associated twisted K3 surfaces have non-trivial Brauer classes. Therefore, these fourfolds are expected to be irrational.
item.dc:creator: Augustinas Jacovskis, Reinder Meinsma, Riccardo Moschetti

item.title: Foliations on abelian surfaces in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.32975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies foliations on abelian surfaces in positive characteristic. We provide an explicit description of all smooth foliations, linear and turbulent, and establish criteria for being $p$-closed. We explicitly determine the moduli spaces of such foliations. We give an application to the construction of $p$-closed foliations, with mild singularities, on Kummer $K3$-surfaces in positive characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Andreatta, Eyal Z. Goren

item.title: Relative Langlands duality for linear periods
item.description: arXiv:2610.31771v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove relative Langlands duality for $X = GL_{p+q}/(GL_p \times GL_q)$. These symmetric spaces arise in the setting of the linear period of Friedberg-Jacquet when $p=q$, and exhibit non-tempered behavior when $q>p+1$. Via the real-symmetric correspondence, we establish a derived Satake equivalence for the real group $G_{\mathbb R}=U(p,q)$, and use it to obtain a constructible realization of coherent sheaves on Kato's exotic nilpotent cones. Along the way, we describe the dual variety of $X$ in terms of the Whittaker cotangent bundle and regular centralizers, viewed as Coulomb branches.
item.dc:creator: Tsao-Hsien Chen, Sanath K. Devalapurkar, Mark Macerato, David Nadler

item.title: On perfectoid ideals
item.description: arXiv:2610.31964v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study perfectoid ideals using the reduction modulo $p$ of perfectoid rings. We show that perfectoid ideals correspond to ideals in the reduction modulo $p$ on which Frobenius is surjective. We establish the existence of universal $p$-adic power series whose evaluations, together with their compatible $p$-power roots, generate perfectoidizations of ideals. In the special case of the perfectoidization of $\mathbb{Z}_p^{\mathrm{cycl}}\langle t^{1/p^{\infty}}\rangle/(t-1)$, we describe a linear algebra algorithm for computing finite approximations of such generators. We illustrate this by an explicit approximation modulo $8$ of an element $\sigma\in (t-1)_{\mathrm{perfd}}\subseteq \mathbb{Z}_2^{\mathrm{cycl}}\langle t^{1/2^{\infty}}\rangle$ which admits compatible sequences of $2$-power roots and satisfies $\sigma\equiv t-1\pmod{2}$.
item.dc:creator: L\'eo Navarro Chafloque

item.title: Singular Loci of SL2(C)-Representation Varieties of Torus Knot Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.32064v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $T(q,p)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle$, where $p,q>1$ are relatively prime, and let \[ R=\Hom(T(q,p),\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)). \] We compute the integral homology of the singular locus of $R$. We show that this locus has complex dimension $2$ and is a disjoint union of $\mu=(p-1)(q-1)$ smooth affine surfaces, each homotopy equivalent to the two-dimensional sphere. Consequently, \[ H_0(\Sing R;\Z)\cong H_2(\Sing R;\Z)\cong\Z^\mu, \] and all remaining homology groups vanish. Thus both nonzero Betti numbers equal the first Betti number of the Milnor fiber of the plane curve singularity $z^p+w^q=0$, namely its Milnor number $\mu$.
item.dc:creator: S. Liriano

item.title: Contributions to the Stable Derived Categories of Gorenstein Rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.32074v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The stable derived category $D_{sg}(R)$ of a Gorenstein ring $R$ is the Verdier quotient of the bounded derived category $D^b(\mathsf{mod}\, R)$ by the thick subcategory of perfect complexes, and was introduced by Buchweitz as a homological measure of the singularities of $R$. This thesis contributes to its study, centered around representation-theoretic and Koszul duality aspects. In Part I, we complete (over $\mathbb{C}$) the classification of homogeneous complete intersection isolated singularities $R$ for which $D^{\mathbb{Z}}_{sg}(R)$ (respectively, $D^b(\mathsf{coh}\, X)$ for $X = \mathsf{proj}\, R$) contains a tilting object. We then use results of Buchweitz-Iyama-Yamaura to describe the indecomposable objects in $D_{sg}^{\mathbb{Z}}(R_Y)$ for $R_Y$ the coordinate rings of $4$ points on $\mathbb{P}^1$ and $4$ points on $\mathbb{P}^2$ in general position, and classify their Betti tables. In Part II, for $R$ a Koszul Gorenstein algebra, we study a natural pair of subcategories whose intersection $\mathcal{H}^{\mathsf{lin}}(R) \subseteq D_{sg}^{\mathbb{Z}}(R)$ consists of modules with eventually linear projective resolutions. We prove that such a pair forms a bounded t-structure if and only if $R$ is absolutely Koszul in the sense of Herzog-Iyengar, in which case $D^b(\mathcal{H}^{\mathsf{lin}}(R)) \cong D_{sg}^{\mathbb{Z}}(R)$. We then relate the heart to modules over the Koszul dual $R^!$. This extends the BGG correspondence to any pair of Koszul dual algebras $(R, R^!)$ with $R$ absolutely Koszul Gorenstein, applying e.g. to elliptic normal curves and del Pezzo surfaces of degree $\geq 4$. Finally, we relate our results to conjectures of Bondal and Minamoto on the graded coherence of AS-regular algebras and higher preprojective algebras; we characterise when these conjectures hold in a restricted setting, and give counterexamples to both in all dimensions $\geq 4$.
item.dc:creator: Vincent G\'elinas

item.title: Meromorphic approximation of holomorphic maps into algebraically elliptic projective varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.32384v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that holomorphic maps from a neighborhood of a compact set in a Stein space to an algebraically elliptic smooth projective variety can be approximated by meromorphic maps, provided that the map extends continuously to the whole space and the compact set is convex with respect to a submonoid of the Picard group. The proof uses algebraic sprays and their polynomial lifts to affine cones, which we call conic lifts. Rational sprays, which generalize algebraic sprays, extend the result to maps avoiding the exceptional set of a rational spray. We also show that, for smooth projective varieties, the existence of an algebraic spray which is dominating at some point is a birational invariant.
item.dc:creator: Yuta Kusakabe, Taichi Miyazaki

item.title: Quivers with Involutions and Shifted affine $\mathrm{i}$Quantum groups via Coulomb Branches
item.description: arXiv:2610.32400v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a formula for quasi-minuscule monopole operators in $K$-theoretic quantized Coulomb branch algebras of cotangent type. We then study signed quivers with involutions, with orthogonal or symplectic gauge factors at the involution-fixed vertices. We construct a GKLO-type homomorphism from the corresponding shifted affine $\mathrm{i}$quantum group to an algebra of $q$-difference operators and prove that it factors through the quantized Coulomb branch algebra. These homomorphisms give geometric realizations of the shifted affine $\mathrm{i}$quantum groups in terms of dressed minuscule and quasi-minuscule monopole operators.
item.dc:creator: Yaolong Shen, Changjian Su, Zichang Wang, Rui Xiong

item.title: Noetherian local rings without perfectoid towers
item.description: arXiv:2610.32577v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$. We prove that if a $p$-torsionfree ring $R$, defined by homogeneous equations over $W(k)$, admits a perfectoid tower arising from $(R,(p))$, then its special fiber is $F$-liftable. We also give explicit examples admitting no such tower, including examples with $F$-liftable special fibers.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuki Yamaguchi

item.title: A genus-two spectral curve of the Riemann $\Xi$-function: Real Structure and Certified Arithmetic Separation of Periods
item.description: arXiv:2610.32694v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We associate a compact genus-two real spectral core with a transverse logarithmic-derivative discriminant of the Riemann $\Xi$-function. Directed interval arithmetic certifies its branch geometry, a real $P_{\mathrm{III}}(D_6)$ scalar-normal-form realization, and associated Kummer and Shioda--Inose models. Zero-action resonance reduces to rationality of two real period ratios. Their certified heat motion yields generic local nonresonance and Diophantine separation, while explicit Farey windows impose denominator barriers of $1{,}036{,}003$ and $140{,}769$ throughout $|\kappa|\le3\times10^{-10}$ in the heat time $\kappa$. Fixed-point irrationality and exact Picard rank remain open. The heat tangent differs from the matched fixed-exponent isomonodromic direction, but admits a local moving-exponent curve lift. Separately, a reciprocal-head canopy certificate combined with published finite-RH and rectangular time-barrier verifications bounds the de Bruijn--Newman constant by $\Lambda\le433/2500=0.1732$ without a QRH assumption. These local arithmetic and global analytic results share a phase--transverse bridge; no equivalence between core nonresonance and RH is asserted.
item.dc:creator: Michel Planat

item.title: Structure and Exact Certification of Nonnegative Tensor Decompositions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32787v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the structure and exact certification of nonnegative tensor decompositions supplied through rational factor matrices. Every failure of minimality or essential uniqueness contains an irreducible positive exchange between $p$ supplied terms and $q$ competing terms. A dimension count based on the Lovitz--Petrov splitting theorem bounds the effective order of such an exchange, the sum over the modes of the joint factor-span dimension minus one, by $p+q-2$, and this bound is attained at every supplied length $R\ge2$. After eliminating ambient-row variables by the Farkas lemma, the resulting semialgebraic systems have fewer than $2R^2$ real variables. For input bit length $L$, this gives a deterministic $G(R)L^{O(R^2)}$-time algorithm that computes the nonnegative rank and an exact minimum-length decomposition, decides minimality and essential uniqueness, and returns exact witnesses when either property fails. The exponent is independent of the tensor order and the mode dimensions. For Lebesgue moment tensors, positive quadrature determines the nonnegative rank and the uniqueness behavior, and some rational length-$R$ inputs force a common field of degree at least $\lfloor R/2\rfloor!$ for any exact minimum-length output. As an illustration, an implementation resolves all 114 instances left inconclusive by earlier positive-scattering criteria, of which 95 are minimal and essentially unique and 19 are minimal but nonunique.
item.dc:creator: Haoming Wang, Ming Yuan

item.title: Atiyah duality for motivic spectra
item.description: arXiv:2403.01561v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that Atiyah duality holds in the $\infty$-category of non-$\mathbb A^1$-invariant motivic spectra over arbitrary derived schemes: every smooth projective scheme is dualizable with dual given by the Thom spectrum of its negative tangent bundle. The Gysin maps recently constructed by L. Tang are a key ingredient in the proof. We then present several applications. First, we study $\mathbb A^1$-colocalization, which transforms any module over the $\mathbb A^1$-invariant sphere into an $\mathbb A^1$-invariant motivic spectrum without changing its values on smooth projective schemes. This can be applied to all known $p$-adic cohomology theories and gives a new elementary approach to "logarithmic" or "tame" cohomology theories; it recovers for instance the logarithmic crystalline cohomology of strict normal crossings compactifications over perfect fields and shows that the latter is independent of the choice of compactification. Second, we prove a motivic Landweber exact functor theorem, associating a motivic spectrum to any graded formal group law classified by a flat map to the moduli stack of formal groups. Using this theorem, we compute the ring of $\mathbb P^1$-stable cohomology operations on the algebraic K-theory of qcqs derived schemes, and we prove that rational motivic cohomology is an idempotent motivic spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Toni Annala, Marc Hoyois, Ryomei Iwasa

item.title: K\"unneth and extension theorems for Morita invariants of non-commutative schemes
item.description: arXiv:2412.08892v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we apply the derived Morita theory of dg-categories to show how to extend the domain of validity of many identities relating Morita invariants from associative dg-algebras toward non-commutative scheme. Doing so, we obtain that the dg-category of associative algebras can be used to test the exactness of any sequence and the commutativity of any diagram involving Morita invariants depending multilinearly on their arguments, under a mild condition of stability by cofibrant replacement. This gives a simple picture of how the underlying algebra of a non-commutative scheme captures its Morita invariant properties. As an application, we use a K\"unneth formula on non-commutative schemes to factorise the Hochschild cohomology of a product of quasi-phantom categories such as built by Orlov and Gorshinsky in [GO13]. This is an occasion to explore how the derived Morita theory interacts with the \v{C}ech dg-enhancement of a projective scheme and to shed an unifying light upon the landscape of dg-modules over dg-categories.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Nicolle

item.title: Intersections of Schubert varieties and smooth $T$-stable subvarieties of flag varieties
item.description: arXiv:2506.21180v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A smooth projective variety equipped with a suitable torus action admits a cell decomposition, called the Bia{\l}ynicki-Birula decomposition. The singularities of the closures of these cells are not well understood in general. Schubert varieties in a flag variety~\(G/B\) are classical examples of such closures, and several criteria for their smoothness are known. In this paper, we study the closures of Bia{\l}ynicki-Birula cells in regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties~\(\mathrm{Hess}(s,h)\), called Hessenberg Schubert varieties. We first investigate the smoothness of intersections of Schubert varieties with \(\mathrm{Hess}(s,h)\), obtaining a sufficient condition for a Hessenberg Schubert variety to be smooth. We also establish several combinatorial sufficient conditions for the smoothness of Hessenberg Schubert varieties in type \(A\).
item.dc:creator: Jaehyun Hong, Eunjeong Lee, Seonjeong Park

item.title: Polar decompositions of complex varieties and tropical homotopy theory
item.description: arXiv:2601.14116v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We take the first steps towards developing a tropical homotopy theory, which we use to construct explicit finite CW complex structures on smooth complex varieties. Our approach decomposes a variety into a set of radial and angular parts, a construction we call polar decomposition. We derive a combinatorial formula for the $f$-vector of the resulting CW complex in terms of a weighted sum of local angle $f$-vectors, and we determine these $f$-vectors explicitly for toric varieties and complete intersections in terms of Stirling numbers. To construct these decompositions, we introduce the notion of a rational tropical manifold, which we view as a tropical manifold with a non-reduced structure. The local topology of these is dictated by Kummer coverings of affine linear spaces in a complex torus, as opposed to the affine linear spaces in the theory of tropical manifolds. Examples of such manifolds include the Fermat and Dwork hypersurfaces. Using Kato-Nakayama spaces, we associate a diagram of topological spaces to any rational tropical manifold. We then construct a cofibrant replacement of this diagram using sealed Kato-Nakayama spaces to show that the homotopy colimit is homotopy equivalent to a general nearby fiber. To construct CW complex structures, we then show that the spaces in the diagram can be replaced by their angle sets. More precisely, for any Kummer covering of a very affine linear space, we prove that the angle map is a homotopy equivalence, extending earlier work of Salvetti and Bj\"{o}rner--Ziegler. We construct compatible cellulations for these angle spaces and show that these give rise to an explicit CW complex structure on the nearby fibers. For complete intersections, we make these spaces and all the CW complex structures completely explicit using refined Coxeter arrangements.
item.dc:creator: Yassine Elmaazouz, Paul Alexander Helminck

item.title: Generalizations of tropical Tevelev degrees
item.description: arXiv:2601.21973v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study tropical Tevelev degrees arising from maps between certain tropical moduli spaces of curves. Building on work of Dawson and Cavalieri, who defined and computed tropical Tevelev degrees in the case of degree $d = g+1$ and $n = g+3$ marked points, we extend the theory by introducing an additional integer parameter $\ell$. In our framework the curve degree and number of marked points vary as $d = g + 1 + \ell$ and $n = g + 3 + 2\ell$, and we analyze the resulting tropical Tevelev degrees for both positive and negative values of $\ell$. This tropicalizes results of Cela, Pandharipande, and Schmitt on algebraic Tevelev degrees. We then further broaden the framework by introducing generalized tropical Tevelev degrees, providing the tropical counterpart to the generalized Tevelev degrees studied by Cela and Lian. These results establish a wider set of computational and structural patterns for intersection calculations on tropical moduli spaces and reveal new behavior beyond the classical setting.
item.dc:creator: Erin Dawson

item.title: Characteristic cycles of real and complex constructible sheaves, revisited
item.description: arXiv:2603.14821v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a smooth morphism $f: X \longrightarrow \Sigma$ of real analytic manifolds and an $\mathbb{R}$-constructible sheaf $F$ on $X$ satisfying some condition, we define a family of Lagrangian cycles parameterized by $\Sigma$ that we call the relative characteristic cycle of $F$ for $f$. In this way, the theory of characteristic cycles due to Kashiwara and Schapira is naturally extended to the relative setting. Based on it, we then prove a formula for the characteristic cycles of real nearby cycle sheaves. This leads us to obtain also formulas for the characteristic cycles of various constructible sheaves, such as specialization, microlocalization, and complex nearby and vanishing cycle sheaves, in a unified manner. In fact, our methods allow us to calculate not only their characteristic cycles but also their microlocal types in many situations. We will illustrate it by various examples.
item.dc:creator: Ren Fernandes, Kazuki Kudomi, Kiyoshi Takeuchi

item.title: Geometric singularities of regular surfaces with nef anti-canonical divisors over imperfect fields
item.description: arXiv:2604.05293v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $S$ be a regular projective surface over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, with $H^0(S,\mathcal{O}_S)=k$ and $-K_S$ nef. We prove that $S$ is geometrically integral over $k$ when $p\geq 7$, and we also find an example of $S$ that is not geometrically integral when $p=5$.
item.dc:creator: Chongning Wang, Lei Zhang

item.title: Bounds on the F-Pure Threshold of Isolated Hypersurface Singularities
item.description: arXiv:2606.04014v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We obtain bounds for the $F$-pure threshold of isolated hypersurface singularities over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic $p$ in terms of classical singularity invariants. For an irreducible plane curve whose value semigroup has first two generators $\beta_0,\beta_1$, we show that the $F$-pure threshold is at most $\frac{1}{\beta_0}+\frac{1}{\beta_1}$ and differs from it by less than $\frac{1}{\gcd(\beta_0,\beta_1)p}$, with equality when certain base-$p$ digits add without carrying, and we give an example showing that higher weighted-order terms can change the $F$-pure threshold. We also conjecture a lower bound in terms of the Milnor number, and prove it for semi-quasi-homogeneous singularities, for all plane curves, and whenever the number of variables exceeds $p$. In particular, it holds in characteristic $2$. As applications, we reprove Igusa's formula for the log canonical threshold of a complex plane branch (with integer coefficients), prove the conjecture of Musta\c{t}\u{a}, Takagi and Watanabe for such branches, and bound the log canonical threshold of complex isolated hypersurface singularities.
item.dc:creator: Yotam Svoray

item.title: Classification of Smooth Minimal K\"ahler Fourfolds Without Effective Divisors and Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.04536v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the following two statements: (1) If $X$ is a compact K\"ahler fourfold with pseudo-effective canonical bundle and no subvarieties of codimension one or two, then $K_X$ is a torsion line bundle; (2) If $X$ is a compact K\"ahler fourfold with no subvarieties of codimension one or two, then $X$ is not uniruled. Using the Beauville-Bogomolov decomposition and a characterization of Uniruled manifolds by Wenhao Ou, we get that if $X$ is a compact K\"ahler fourfold with no subvarieties of codimension one or two, then either $X$ is a torus or an irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifold.
item.dc:creator: Pisya Vikash

item.title: Remarks on the monodromy conjecture for symmetric determinantal hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.18395v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the local and global Denef--Loeser topological zeta functions of the determinant on the space of symmetric matrices. It verifies the strong monodromy conjecture of the symmetric determinant function. The computation relates to the geometry of complete quadrics and wonderful embeddings.
item.dc:creator: Renjie Lyu, Xiping Zhang

item.title: Positivity for toric Kac polynomials in higher depth
item.description: arXiv:2310.02912v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the polynomials counting locally free, absolutely indecomposable, rank 1 representations of quivers over rings of truncated power series have non-negative coefficients. This generalizes the positivity of toric Kac polynomials to higher depth. The proof goes by inductively contracting/deleting arrows of the quiver and is inspired by a previous work of Abdelgadir, Mellit and Rodriguez-Villegas on toric Kac polynomials. We also relate counts of absolutely indecomposable quiver representations in higher depth and counts of jets over fibres of quiver moment maps. This is expressed as a plethystic identity involving generating series of these counts. In rank 1, we prove a cohomological upgrade of this identity, by computing the compactly supported cohomology of jet spaces over preprojective stacks. This is reminiscent of PBW isomorphisms for preprojective cohomological Hall algebras. Finally, our plethystic identity allows us to prove two conjectures by Wyss on the asymptotic behavior of both counts, when depth goes to infinity.
item.dc:creator: Tanguy Vernet

item.title: Symmetries and Higher-Form Connections in Derived Differential Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2602.03441v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a general definition of higher-form connections on principal $\infty$-bundles in differential geometry. These connections are built as infinitesimal parallel transports and thus satisfy the fake-curvature condition. We achieve this by developing the formal differentiation and integration of maps from smooth manifolds to derived stacks with sufficient deformation theory. That allows us to introduce the Atiyah $L_\infty$-algebroid of a principal $\infty$-bundle and establish its global sections as the $L_\infty$-algebra of the derived higher symmetry group of the bundle. We define the space of $p$-form connections on an $\infty$-bundle as the space of order $p$ splittings of its Atiyah $L_\infty$-algebroid. This can be cast equivalently as lifting the classifying map of a bundle on a manifold to the order $p$ truncation of the de Rham stack of the manifold. We demonstrate that our new concept of derived geometric $p$-form connections recovers the known notion of connections on higher U(1)-bundles defined via \v{C}ech-Deligne differential cocycles. We further relate the $L_\infty$-algebras of derived higher symmetries of higher U(1)-bundles and higher Courant algebroids. Some applications in higher gauge theory and in supergravity are mentioned.
item.dc:creator: Severin Bunk, Lukas M\"uller, Joost Nuiten, Richard J. Szabo

item.title: Oka Geometry of Complex Six-Spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.00250v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Alp\"oge constructed a complex structure on $S^6$ through a torus fibration with exactly three special fibres. We prove that every member of the associated admissible period family is Oka and that the family projection over each relatively compact parameter disc is an Oka map. The Oka property survives the deletion or simultaneous blow-up of any finite set of distinct points in any member. Blowing up a single point therefore produces an Oka complex manifold diffeomorphic, but not biholomorphic, to $\mathbb{P}^3$. The proofs combine explicit cyclic coverings with analytic extension and the invariance of the Oka property under holomorphic coverings.
item.dc:creator: Yun-Heng Du, Bin Guo, Yuta Kusakabe, Song-Yan Xie

item.title: Christoffel transformations of symmetric $d$-connections and gap probability recurrences
item.description: arXiv:2610.28497v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the Christoffel transformation $w(x)\mapsto x^2w(x)$ of an even discrete weight. For the associated orthogonal polynomial ensembles on squared nodes $y=x^2$, ratios of moment determinants relate the largest-particle distributions and transfer exact gap probability recurrences between the ensembles. For positive weights satisfying the stated moment and support assumptions, this comparison requires no Pearson condition. The transformation is realized by elementary bundle modifications at zero and infinity on $\mathbb P^1$. When the original weight has Pearson ratio $d(-z-1)/d(z)$ with $\mathrm{deg}\; d=1,2$, these modifications conjugate cutoff dynamics on common stable loci of symmetric $d$-connections under the stated geometric hypotheses. The transformed recurrence coefficients are expressed explicitly as rational functions of spectral coordinates. On the unit lattice, a local recurrence formula applies to rational symmetric Pearson ratios of arbitrary degree, including outside these charts, whenever its local hypotheses hold.
item.dc:creator: Anton Selemenchuk
